subject: Exception conditions
notes: Rule: §14.6.13.1.3 3) (cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.3 "If the exception condition is a fatal EC-I-O exception condition, then the rules for 9.1.13, I-O status apply" -> OK 3)). A fatal EC-I-O condition first runs §9.1.13's processing (the status, the statement's phrase, the applicable exception processing statements of §9.1.12 / §14.9.49 - at most one declarative: §14.9.49.4 GR3 'The first declarative that satisfies the selection criteria is executed and no other declaratives are executed', cite.py OK 3)), then the remaining fatal rules (#7). Code: __IoCheckEc sets the status (SetIo), consults the WHEN frame, then the F1 file/open-mode tiers, then the F3 tiers only if nothing was selected, then throws CobolFatalException for a fatal status class with checking enabled unless a RESUME redirected. No implementor 'otherwise' is specified. Probes out/probe/exc-fatal: f2 (>>TURN EC-I-O ON, OPEN INPUT of a missing file, F1 USE ON F plus F3 USE AFTER EC EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR) -> 'F1-DECL 35 EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR' then abnormal termination, exit 1; f3 (same, no TURN) -> 'F1-DECL 35 / AFTER-OPEN 35', exit 0 (the §9.1.13.1 continue latitude with checking off). The named test pins the enabled no-handler termination. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (EC model introduced by ISO 2002; the §9.1.13 I-O status rules themselves predate it)
